Build a multi-page personal portfolio website using plain HTML, CSS, and
JavaScript (no frameworks), ready to host on GitHub Pages.

About me: I'm Raul , a First year bachelor student studying computer engineering at Ada University in
Azerbaijan. 

Pages:
1. index.html (Home): profile photo, a short first-person intro (3-4 sentences),
   and buttons linking to Projects and About.
2. about.html: my background, education, qualifications/certificates, skills,
   and activities (clubs, volunteering, competitions, hobbies, not only this course).
3. projects.html: a card for each project with title, description, and a
   screenshot/photo gallery. Required: Project 1 (Logic Gates), Project 2 (Hour of
   Code), Project 3 (Robotics).  resume.html or contact.html.

Every page must have:
- The same navigation bar (highlight the current page, hamburger menu on mobile)
- The same footer (copyright, email, social icons)
- A GitHub icon linking to https://github.com/raul091r/raul091r.github.io
- Optional icons: LinkedIn, email, Instagram

Repository structure:
/
├── index.html
├── pages/ (about.html, projects.html, ...)
├── assets/
│   ├── css/ (base.css, layout.css, components.css, pages.css)
│   ├── js/ (nav.js, gallery.js, main.js)
│   └── images/ (profile/, projects/)
├── README.md
└── .gitignore

Code requirements: semantic HTML, CSS variables for colors and fonts, no inline
styles, no duplicated CSS, commented JS, responsive and accessible (alt text,
good contrast, keyboard-friendly nav). Use placeholder images that I can
replace, with clear file names.

Writing requirements: Write all website text in my voice, like a real student, not a marketing brand.
Rules:
- Use first person and plain, specific language.
- Banned words and phrases: passionate, driven, dynamic, cutting-edge,
  leverage, journey, dive into, in today's world, unlock, tapestry, seamless,
  "I am a [adjective] individual".
- Prefer concrete details over claims: what I built, what broke, what I
  learned, numbers, names, dates.
- Vary sentence length. Short sentences are fine. No lists of three adjectives.
- Leave [PLACEHOLDER: what to fill in] where you'd need my real details instead
  of inventing them.
